lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's grow and shrink a running cluster.
Your test needs more nodes, or you want to see what happens when one leaves. sind adds and removes workers while the cluster keeps running.
Run sind create worker, and you get one more worker, just like the newest one.
The count flag adds several at once. Here, three more.
For each managed worker, sind creates the container, adds a node definition, reconfigures slurmctld, and then starts slurmd on it.
If a step fails, sind removes the new containers, so you can simply try again.
New workers copy the newest worker: its image, its CPU and memory limits, and its capabilities and devices.
Each flag you give replaces the inherited value. This worker gets a CPU limit of two, and one gigabyte of memory.
To remove workers, give sind delete worker a node set, here workers two to four.
sind takes them out of the Slurm configuration first, and then deletes their containers.
So: create worker copies the newest worker, flags override what it inherits, and delete worker updates Slurm before it removes the containers.
Next up: Power Control, where nodes crash on purpose. See you there!
